title: Triceps Strength Following Olecranon Fracture Fixation
official: A Randomized Controlled Trial Assessing Triceps Strength Following Olecranon Fracture Fixation Using a Triceps Tendon Sparing Plate vs Triceps Tendon Split Plate
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to compare two types of plates used to surgically treat olecranon fractures, which are fractures of the bony point of the elbow. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does a plate that preserves the triceps tendon result in better triceps strength than a plate that requires splitting the triceps tendon?
* Are there differences in elbow movement and function between the two treatments?

Researchers will compare participants treated with a short-flange plate that preserves the triceps tendon with participants treated with a long-flange plate that requires splitting the triceps tendon.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of the two surgical treatment groups
* Undergo surgical fixation of their olecranon fracture using the assigned plate
* Have their elbow strength and range of motion measured during follow-up
* Complete questionnaires about arm function, elbow function, general health, and pain during follow-up
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age 18 years or older
* Isolated, acute, simple displaced olecranon fracture (Mayo Type 2-A)
* Presenting for treatment at a participating study site

Exclusion Criteria:

* Comminuted (multi-fragment) olecranon fracture
* Polytrauma
* Previous triceps injury
* Previous olecranon fracture
* Complication requiring reoperation
